column1: # Supervisor command corpus for the PreToolUse hook (gate_rules.check_tool_call).
# Real readers: bash and dash (the image installs both). zsh is not a reader of these commands.
# Columns: id, expect, command. The command is written with Python escapes (\n is a newline,
# \r a carriage return, \x0c a form feed); the test decodes it.
# expect is what a print-only ha stub received when the shells ran the command:
#   su:<shells>     a Supervisor family (su, super, supervisor) ran: refused in both modes.
#   remote:<shells> only a remote family (host, core, ...) ran: refused with remote control on.
#   none            no family ran in either shell: no answer is required.
#                   a family ran, and the hook lets it pass: a limit that DOCS.md states. The shells must
#                   still run it and the hook must still let it pass; when the hook comes to refuse one,
#                   change its kind to su or remote and change the texts with it.
# test_supervisor_corpus.py runs every command again under bash and dash (as the user the tests
# run as, never root in CI) and checks that each shell named in this column still gives its answer,
# then that the hook refuses each su and remote case. A shell may run a family on another machine
# where none is recorded (dash runs time ha ... only where a time program is installed); the hook
# is then held to the stricter answer. Add a case here; never delete one.
# Sources: reviewer-* and closer-* were written by reviewers of the redirection fix; reduced-* are
# the forms a closer found that passed the hook; fuzz-* are 21 prefixes x 21 middles x 2 families
# and single lines aimed at each branch of the rule. Families of hostile input: joined operators,
# quoted or escaped operators and targets, words that expand to nothing ($x, ${x:+}, $(...),
# backticks, {,}, nullglob), line breaks Python reads and the shell does not (\r, \x0c, \x0b,
# \x1c, \x85, U+2028), nested shells, wrappers, continuations and comments.
# closer3-* and closer4-* are the third closure's two sets (quotes on the family word, words the shell
# builds, braces with quoted blanks and operators, globs that match a file). Size: one long word or a
# long command is in the timing tests of test_gate_quote.py, not here (the hook's answer must come in time).
# closer5-* and closer6-* are the fourth closure's two sets (a brace word inside a quoted script that a second
# shell reads: bash -c, eval, trap, a pipe into bash; a built family word behind while, until, else, setsid and
# other words before ha). builder5-* are the fix's own cases, with allowed commands that look hostile (jq filters).
# closer7-* and closer8-* are the fifth closure's two sets (a brace word cut at a quoted blank, a brace word made of
# quoted pieces or an escaped brace for a second shell, a quoted blank before a built family word, extended globs,
# $'...' scripts with escapes, ls -ha and du -ha). Commands already in the corpus are not repeated.
# closer9-* and closer10-* are the sixth closure's two sets. Their passes are the stated limits (su-limit,
# remote-limit): an odd quote in a comment or a heredoc body before ha, a brace word for a second shell with an
# escaped brace and a quoted blank (eval ha \{-x'" y"',s}u info), the program word in the $'...' form, a
# built family word in a nested backtick, and an unknown flag with a quoted blank (ha -x"a b" su info, which
# the real ha refuses to run). Six commands that printf or echo -e builds for a second shell are left out, as
# below. closer11-* to closer13-* are the seventh closure's three sets (a value flag with = and an empty
# value, an empty word of several quoted pieces, a flag value that the shell removes, then a built family
# word); their one pass is the odd-quote limit above. closer14-* and closer15-* are the eighth closure's two
# sets (a flag value of one character that Python reads as a blank and the shell reads as a letter, a removed
# flag value before a flag, a redirection or another value pair, a nullglob or {,} value, a quoted script in two
# pieces or after an escaped quote, a variable that holds the flag value and the family word); closerws-* are
# that closure's white space probe (18 characters in 7 forms). closer16-* and closer17-* are the ninth closure's
# two sets (a value with an odd blank and then a quote, a variable value after a redirection, and the forms
# that the closure found outside the rules). Their passes are stated limits: a family word that is not whole
# in the text (v='x s'; ha --log-level ${v}u info, or a $ joined to the flag), a quoted script with a piece
# outside quotes (eval 'setsid ha' --log-level '"" s${x}u info'), a nested brace word, an extended glob with
# nullglob, a redirection before a second flag's value, and a brace word or a glob that holds the value and
# the family word (touch a su; ha --log-level * info). closer18-* and closer19-* are the tenth closure's two sets
# (an odd blank in each place of the white space rules, a redirection joined to a value flag, a process
# substitution as the target). Their passes are the stated limit of an unknown flag with a quoted blank
# (setsid ha --foo<CR>"a b" su info). closer20-* is the eleventh closure's set (a redirection between a value
# flag and its value whose target holds a quoted or escaped operator character, a quoted blank or a
# n/a: Unicode look-alike letters (ha is a fixed ASCII program name; the shell does not fold them);
# aliases and functions (DOCS names them as a limit: the check reads text, not shell state).
# Left out on purpose, as limits DOCS states (the check cannot see a program that the command builds or that
# another program runs): h${x}a su info, h$(:)a su info, {ha,su} info, {ha,su,info}, {ha,} su info,
# echo su info | xargs ha, a base64 text piped into sh, python3 -c and perl -e that run ha, an alias,
